title: Estimated vs actual rows: stale statistics
claim: If the database thinks it is processing 100 rows but actually processes 100,000, its optimization decisions
will be terrible. Large discrepancies often point to outdated statistics.
verdict: Confirmed, dramatically. With statistics from before the new consumer's 1M rows, the planner estimated a few
hundred rows, fetched all 1,000,000 through the consumer index and sorted them ({t:stale}). After ANALYZE (0.2
s) it expects 1M rows, walks the date index backwards and stops after 20 ({t:fresh}): {x:stale/fresh} faster.
Autovacuum re-analyzes only after about 10% of a table changes, so bulk loads and new tenants can outrun it: run
